Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Shatrughna Yadav, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that on 28.07.2023 notice has been served to the informant of the case.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

2. Heard Sri R.O.V.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Shatrughna Yadav, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
176 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station- Ajeetmal, District- Auraiya, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and one Musku and according to the FIR,
applicant and co-accused Musku tried to commit rape with the daughter of the informant aged Shivendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154034108/
1 about 13 years.

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that initially FIR of the present case was lodged under Sections 354, 504, 506 IPC 7/8 POCSO Act but subsequently after the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. case was converted under Section 376 IPC.
6.

He further submitted that although, prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but when her statement was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. then she stated that applicant and co-accused Musku both committed rape with her and this fact clearly suggests that she is not a reliable witness.

7. He further submitted that during investigation involvement of the co-accused Musku was found false and therefore, no charge-sheet was filed against him and charge-sheet was filed only against the applicant.

He further submitted that during investigation police informer informed the Investigating Officer that totally on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been roped in the present matter but in spite of that charge-sheet has been filed against him.
8. He further submitted that applicant has been roped in the present matter due to village party bandi and he is not having any criminal history and is in jail since 02.06.2023.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that prosecutrix was hardly thirteen and half years' old at the time of incident and she in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant and applicant failed to bring any good reason for his false implication, therefore, he does not deserve bail.
10. I have heard both the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. From the record, it reflects that prosecutrix was hardly thirteen and half years' old at the time of incident and she made allegation of rape against the applicant in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. although, in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she did not make allegation of rape against co-accused Musku and she made allegation of rape against applicant and co-accused Musku in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
but consistently she made allegation of rape against the applicant therefore, at this stage, no benefit can be extended in favour of the applicant.
Further, applicant failed to bring any good reason for his false implication on record.

12. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
13. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected.

14. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the Shivendra Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154034108/
